name: I Beograd City Park Race/beograd Gp

nar.text: The 50,000 spectators, aware that Germany had attacked Poland two days ago, knew since this Sunday morning, that Great Britain and France in support of Poland, were at war with Germany.
Only five cars start: two Mercedes, two Auto Unions and Milenković's 1925 Bugatti.
At the 4:45 p.m. start Lang intended to be very quick but had rear-wheel shatter, enabling von Brauchitsch to shoot into the lead. A furious Lang tried to pass, only to be pushed onto the pavement.
Brauchitsch leads Lang, Nuvolari, Müller and Milenković.
Brauchitsch was driving very wild, with Lang glued to his tail, looking for a chance to pass. Neubauer waved his house-flag, but Manfred maintained his wild style.
On lap 6 Brauchitsch had taken one of the corners too fast, his car slid to the road edge and his rear wheels threw up a burst of little stones.
One stone shattered the wind-screen of Lang's Mercedes and both glasses of his goggles.
Lang, blinded, pulls over to let Müller and Nuvolari by, then drives slowly to the pits with a bleeding eye.
Reserve driver Bäumer is ordered into Lang's car, now two laps down.
Bäumer rejoins just behind Brauchitsch, ahead of the two Auto Unions.
Bäumer hits a poplar tree; the car is out, the driver unhurt.
Brauchitsch leads Müller, who has gone by Nuvolari.
Brauchitsch sets a new lap record of 1m14.0s.
Brauchitsch, 13.8 seconds clear, spins at an uphill right-hander and stalls facing the wrong way.
The car faced the wrong way and by letting his car roll downhill in the wrong direction, he was able to re-start.
Müller and Nuvolari swerve around the Mercedes as it turns back; Müller leads.
Müller leads by five seconds from Nuvolari, with Brauchitsch eight seconds back.
Müller equals the lap record of 1m14.0s.
Müller's left rear tyre breaker flies off; he limps to the pits and Nuvolari leads.
Nuvolari leads Brauchitsch by five seconds.
Brauchitsch stops with shattered rear tyres.
Nuvolari, 50 seconds ahead, stops for fuel and tyres in 26 seconds and is push-started.
Neubauer wants to protest the push start; Auto Union points to Brauchitsch's earlier wrong-way restart.
Nuvolari rejoins eight seconds ahead of Brauchitsch.
Brauchitsch hunts Nuvolari but gets no closer than eight seconds.
Milenković's Bugatti has been lapped many times.
Nuvolari wins by 7.6 seconds from Brauchitsch, with Müller 30.6 seconds back; Milenković is flagged off 19 laps down.
